<a id="выполнение-задачи"></a>

# Execute the task

For an incidental environment/tool failure, use Fixer (`procedures/fix.md` in the active release): restore the original action, record useful reusable knowledge and continue.

Execute the task route (`procedures/task.md#choose-a-sufficient-route` in the active release) within authority. Keep one primary source for requirements and tasks. For a chain, continue Planner (`procedures/planner.md` in the active release) state. Change authorized scope and maintain affected documents and archive. Choose checks below. Before completion, compare mandatory criteria with current results or explicit gaps.

CI is asynchronous. Complete local checks/review; report available exact-SHA CI separately. Pending/unavailable CI does not block authorized progression. Diagnose known failure and fix the actual defect. Wait only under an explicit project/user condition; a workflow alone creates no barrier.

<a id="доказательства-и-ревью"></a>

## Evidence and review

For a significant check, save command, scope, code and dependency state, time, tool, result and the original machine report link. Add logs/screenshots when useful; do not copy the report into a task archive. Read routine evidence through `spec-read --view evidence --id HG-ID`. Open original reports for targeted review or diagnosis. Before an expensive run, finalize common rules, configuration, version and the checked chain scope. After checked logic/tests/configuration change, repeat affected checks. Reuse unchanged results across work, commit and push.

Before spec-evidence, finish the real check and original report and preserve review inputs. Do not edit a recorded report for notes. Record cleanup separately when it does not change the checked result. Changed input/observation needs new affected evidence; changing the overall task revision alone does not.

Scenario-test links, exit codes and execution are separate facts. For a manual exercise, preserve initial conditions and observation limits. Skipped, unknown and stale remain gaps. A previous exception applies only to its own conditions.

Independent review is mandatory for product behavior, access/data preservation, architecture boundaries, core workflow rules or a user request. Small edits with unchanged requirements need only executor checks. Early findings are allowed; request a final verdict after implementation, local checks and available evidence records. At review, read the method (`references/review.md` in the active release) and assign a separate subagent. Supply exact requirements/scenarios, relevant diff, original reports, declared inputs, limits and readiness criteria. Obtain GO or NO_GO with specific findings. After material fixes, request review of the new revision. Unavailable mandatory review leaves work unfinished. Self-review is not independent GO. Review does not replace tests.

<a id="содержательные-проверки"></a>

## Substantive checks

Check the real changed logic, not a simplified duplicate. Isolate expensive/unstable boundaries as needed. Transactions, storage, queues and UI require checking their actual boundary. A significant fixed defect gets a reproducible regression scenario when risk warrants it. Control inputs, clocks, randomness and external responses where needed for reproduction. No separate DSL/simulator is required.

| Change | Sufficient check | Reason to expand |
|---|---|---|
| Instruction edit with unchanged meaning | Diff, links and applicable structural check | Meaning drift or specific risk |
| New workflow/authority rule | Independent semantic review and decision table | Execution question unresolved by reading |
| CLI, format or data preservation | Standard contract tests for behavior and material failures | Shared boundary or compatibility |
| Installation/update | Automatic isolated-profile tests | New switching/recovery risk |
| Actual agent actions | Observation on an authorized task | Material question not covered more cheaply |

Small edits need no new behavior tests or improvised agent pilots. An installer/CLI fixture checks code and is not an agent pilot. Text review proves the rule's content, not reliable model execution. State untested behavior as a limit.

The project defines commands and mandatory full barriers. Check affected behavior first, then final-state barriers. Reuse current coverage across stages without omitting independent coverage. After failure, repeat the affected check; repeat a full barrier if its inputs changed.

Choose a narrow behavior test with project barriers and independent coverage in mind. Expand or state a gap for unknown scenario mapping, shared risk or changed inputs. Explain omissions. Routine execution needs no separate planning/profiling. For JSON checks or direct spec-evidence, read the verification reference (`references/tools/verification.md#check-bindings-and-explicit-execution` in the active release) before checking. Run automatic checks through spec-run or import JUnit with an input snapshot **before** execution. Execute manual checks (`runner: null`) by their assigned method and record spec-evidence. If a scenario includes manual checks, complete automatic runs and manual checks before one final direct evidence record; a later run requires updating it. For automatic-only checks, runs/import and CLI records suffice. Without a JSON specification, use standard project checks and original reports. Verify the real test/observation and report. Read timing statistics only for observed slowness; they do not select tests or replace spec-check. Change execution method only for measured benefit with unchanged coverage.

<a id="проверка-до-изменения-реализации"></a>

### Check before implementation changes

For new/changed automatic behavior, normally select or prepare a narrow check of the agreed outcome before implementation. Derive expectations from the contract and check the real product boundary. Reuse a suitable test and current result if they already establish the initial condition.

For a bugfix, reproduce the violation before fixing. For a feature, confirm missing behavior. If an interface is absent, a minimal runnable stub without the main implementation is valid. Then check the expected outcome. A compile error, environment fault, bad selector, skip or empty set is not behavior evidence. Fix preparation or justify another method under the matrix.

Proceed in small parts: check → implementation → successful run → structural improvement while keeping the outcome. Add full-suite tests as work develops. No test per ID, commit or full run per cycle is required. Final project barriers remain.

Save command and observed initial failure cause in the original report. It remains development history; never rename failed to passed. Final successful verification with current inputs confirms the product scenario. Original reports are immutable; material changes require another affected check.

If the test already passes, decide whether the behavior exists or the check is insufficient. Do not break correct code artificially. A behavior-preserving refactor can use a suitable current initial result and successful final check. For research, unstable automation, manual outcomes or normative text, choose a proportionate method and order and briefly explain why. After a bounded authorized trial, define behavior/checks before main implementation. An exception does not remove final criteria or turn text review into agent observation.

<a id="исполнение-сценария"></a>

### Execute a scenario

For each affected scenario, identify initial condition, action and observable outcome. Select a real check that detects its violation. Confirm the test actually ran and asserted that outcome. Standard scripts, browser tests, JUnit and CLI tests remain automatic regardless of trace support. Outside trace, save the actual command and original report. With JSON, use method=native_report for direct automatic evidence below; without a specification, include the report in the task result. State the trace boundary. Exit 0, ID markers or report existence do not close a skipped, empty or unrelated check. One run can cover several scenarios when each outcome is checked separately.

Distinguish automatic reports, direct agent observation and user testimony. For your observation, record setup, action, result, date, version and limits. method=manual is not human acceptance. For a human-only observation, use their message and mark it as reported by the user. Clarify version/actions only if unknown. Activation authority or acceptance does not prove scenario execution. Without observation, leave a gap; do not automatically repeat a human check. New observations get new immutable reports.

Choose repeat/cancel/timeout/event-order checks from the contract, without a fixed quota. For a significant new rule, ensure when practical that the check detects its violation. For agent procedures, check actions, write boundaries and outcome. One run does not establish statistical model reliability. Before an expensive exercise, check isolation, cwd, session feature support, input format and expected result. Correct faulty setup before main execution. Save the full original log, but load only status, material errors and its path into working context. Read details when needed.

<a id="область-входов-доказательства"></a>

### Evidence input scope

Trace each scenario's causal inputs: executed implementation, test/data, configuration, shared modules and dependencies. Keep the full-run snapshot separately. Do not copy the whole src/tests/kit tree into each scenario merely because checks ran together. A neighboring document or report file list change does not require repeating an independent scenario. Keep conservative coverage until an unknown dependency is resolved. Narrowing previous broad inputs needs dependency analysis and a new actual observation; do not rewrite old evidence. Preserve the original shared-report link. For normative review, inputs are reviewed rules and material dependencies, not all executable CLI code.

Integration records historical inclusion of requirements. technical describes evidence freshness for current inputs. in_progress after drift does not automatically mean broken implementation. Human acceptance cannot refresh a stale test. Update only actually reconfirmed results.

<a id="передача-и-продолжение"></a>

## Handoff and continuation

| Stage | Minimum result |
|---|---|
| task | Goal, scope, material decisions and observable behavior |
| spec | Checked requirements, scenarios and evidence methods |
| work | Changes, current checks, required review and explicit gaps |
| commit | Exact local commit; candidate/readiness, activation and acceptance separately |
| push | Range and remote SHA; CI/PR, remainder and return to Work when needed |

Keep accepted decisions, completed work, evidence links and one next step in the primary task artifact. Session state links it without duplicating specification tasks. After interruption, compare state with actual diff and input freshness. Continue from the first unfinished action without repeating accepted questions. Changed scope, lost verification or a new material choice reopens only the dependent part. An open mandatory final criterion prevents Work completion but allows authorized candidate Commit/Push for remote CI/PR under the project pre-submit barrier. After sending, check remote SHA and available CI without mandatory waiting. Fix identified defects within authority and finish remaining criteria. CI, publication and acceptance remain separate states.

<a id="работа-с-json-спецификацией"></a>

## Work with a JSON specification

This applies when a relevant JSON specification exists. Before catalog edits, read structure/operations (`references/tools/specifications.md#structured-specifications` in the active release). For a bugfix, use existing requirements/scenarios, check regression and update review. spec-run/spec-run-import already record automatic evidence. Direct spec-evidence is needed for additional manual work or a separate observation, without a pointless duplicate. Do not rewrite completed tasks/contracts just to track a fix. New results may make prior acceptance stale; never transfer it automatically. For an earlier format, follow the project route. Without a specification, do not call spec-check/integrate/decide.

Read tasks/questions with spec-read --view summary and repeat-work reasons with spec-check --brief true. If an earlier answer or return comment is absent from context, read the original message or selected attention through spec-read --id ID --view full before another question/dependent action. Summary/brief do not contain answers. Check the answer's subject and applicability to the current revision. Do not transfer a stale decision. Refine questions/task from the actual decision; do not invent answers, acceptance or authority. Load full changes/individual requirements for a specific reason, never the whole store. spec-validate checks the contract; spec-check checks execution completeness.

For direct spec-evidence, choose inputs/report before checking under the format (`references/tools/verification.md#checks-and-evidence` in the active release). After actual execution/observation, record method, command, time, scenario, outcome, report and all causal inputs. Compare their before/after states; changed inputs need affected rechecks. spec-evidence hashes files but neither runs tests nor certifies results. Use trace too for supported native reports. skipped/failed/unknown/timeout never become passed. Exclude noncausal administrative state from normative files/inputs. The store is not an input; the tool records its revision. Never exclude material inputs.

For a new change, mark actual completed tasks through spec-edit with CAS and record independent spec-review under Evidence and review above. Include original_text for imports. Changed contracts/material evidence need another review; equivalent repeats do not. After all final criteria, run spec-integrate --brief true; it checks readiness itself. Use a preliminary spec-check only to diagnose reasons. spec-transfer (`references/tools/specifications.md#ids-versions-and-acceptance` in the active release) of an earlier contract preserves its technical gap. For integrated specifications, update results/review then spec-check; never spec-save or integrate again. Commit, push and acceptance remain separate actions.

On base drift, do not adjust baseline/expectations for a green result. Reread the contract, abandon the replaced draft with a reason, and create a change for the agreed result. On concurrent edits, reread and merge deliberately. Keep stale evidence as history, not current scenario confirmation.

<a id="передача-человеку-и-фиксация-решения"></a>

## Handoff to a human and decision recording

Without Git, use the project-assigned immutable result and storage method. Git absence neither prevents verified completion nor authorizes git init.

For a supported specification, hand off a technically ready result through spec-attention (`references/tools/specifications.md#explicit-human-requests` in the active release) kind=result. The system records specification, evidence and checked-input snapshots. An already known exact Git SHA/immutable build ID may be saved as optional verified_revision; the form reuses it. Its absence does not block local acceptance. Do not create a commit, build, extra explanation or LLM call for the form. Do not claim dirty-tree HEAD as verified revision. The answer retains readiness barriers and closes requests for the same snapshot. A returned result may have no comment; do not guess its cause. Requirements agreement is not result acceptance. A fixable technical error alone does not create a request.

Technically ready tasks proceed without awaiting acceptance of each. Without a specification, pass result, checks and limits without invented IDs/commands. Use existing results and original limits for acceptance. Avoid overwhelming the main text with administrative versions/paths, but retain material limits. No extra summary or fixed action count is required for the form. Keep the primary artifact and result snapshots without a second specification.

On an explicit decision about the shown verified snapshot, record spec-decide under the CLI schema (`references/tools/specifications.md#ids-versions-and-acceptance` in the active release), with supplied hashes and author/decision source. Comment and known SHA/build ID are optional. Do not guess a person's name. One batch may cover explicitly selected tasks; clarify only ambiguity. Do not infer acceptance from silence, a plan, tests or review. Do not decide for a human. On drift, use spec-check --brief true to show the changed input and present a new ready snapshot; the previous decision remains historical. Equivalent repeats preserve acceptance; material changes need a new decision. Changed requirements/scenarios in an integrated change require a new change; implementation fixes update results. Acceptance does not authorize commit, push or activation. Project final barriers remain.

<a id="сохранность-результата-при-передаче"></a>

### Preserve a handed-off result

Agree the minimum original reports and unrecoverable inputs with the storage owner. For an authorized handoff, check selected content, including untracked/ignored evidence, through delivery diagnostics (`references/tools/diagnostics.md#evidence-delivery-contents` in the active release). A local file is not yet in a delivery package. For external links, verify project access/storage rules; no automatic upload is assigned. Without a handoff request, no new barrier exists. Local readiness and human acceptance remain distinct.

<a id="завершение-хранения"></a>

### Finish storage

Before the final result, complete project export/maintenance. Save only the necessary original set, check integrity/links, then clean completed temporary runs. Reuse equivalent results. Preserve unknown data, active work and the only needed evidence. Name any material remainder and reason. Without a storage route, do not substitute arbitrary deletion. Keep temporary logs out of normal context and permanent documents.
